articles.title: Motorcycle passenger who took stunning cricket catch found
articles.description: Mehran Khan amazed sports fans around the world when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle.

articles.title: A renovation was meant to improve these Hong Kong homes - it ended in a blaze that killed 168
articles.description: A year after one of Hong Kong's deadliest fires, families left behind are still waiting for justice.

articles.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle legal battle over French winery
articles.description: The Hollywood A-listers' legal battle focused on the vineyard they bought in 2008 and where they wed six years later.

articles.title: Lammens howler denies Man Utd victory against Sporting in incident-packed game
articles.description: Goalkeeper Senne Lammens endures a topsy-turvy night as Manchester United draw with Sporting.controversial decisions.

articles.title: Mexico Investigates Possible Cartel Links of Prosecutor Who Aided C.I.A.
articles.description: The prosecutor recently fled to the United States after Mexico issued a warrant over his involvement with the C.I.A. Now authorities are investigating him for suspected cartel collusion.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay to Host Revival of BBC’s ‘Top Gear’
articles.description: The British car show “Top Gear” paused production three years ago and is returning with a new host in 2028, the BBC said.

articles.title: Lukoil to Sell Foreign Assets, but Not to Kushner and Witkoff Associates
articles.description: Valuable properties belonging to the Russian energy giant will be sold to an American-led consortium. But Middle Eastern business contacts of the two Trump envoys pulled out because of political winds.

articles.title: Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a true Wild Boy
articles.description: How a wayward child from the north-east of England made it with the world's biggest band.

articles.title: Road Fire Near Cairo Kills Dozens After Petroleum-Laden Truck Crashes
articles.description: The blaze killed at least 31 and injured at least 21 near Giza, beside the Nile River, officials said.

articles.title: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
articles.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in a long-running trial that has divided the country. He denies all wrongdoing.

articles.title: Island Paradise of Mauritius Has Sun, Beaches and Too Many Dogs
articles.description: Mauritius, a popular tourist destination off southern Africa, has become overrun with strays. With more and more residents chased and attacked, many are fed up.

articles.title: Libyan Forces Threaten Retaliation Over Ukraine’s Attack on Russian Ships
articles.description: The Ukrainian drone strike off Libya’s coast killed two Libyan naval officers, according to the forces controlling the country’s east.

articles.title: Opposition Makes Progress Toward Ousting Netanyahu, Party Leader Says
articles.description: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, has set Dec. 6 as the deadline to form a new Israeli government. His ally, Avigdor Liberman, said Mr. Eisenkot was on track.

articles.title: Japan’s Leader, in Break With U.S., Defends International Criminal Court
articles.description: Sanae Takaichi welcomed the court’s president and vowed to accelerate financial support despite an effort by the Trump administration to cripple the global body.

articles.title: 2 Men Charged After Break-In at Prince William and Kate’s Country Home
articles.description: Prosecutors said the two men, who appeared in court on Wednesday, had climbed a drainpipe to break into the royals’ country retreat in Norfolk.

articles.title: North Korea Kicks Out Swiss Diplomats in Spat Linked to Ukraine War
articles.description: The move followed Switzerland’s decision to impose sanctions on an international youth camp in North Korea, which is accused of hosting Ukrainian children for indoctrination.

articles.title: Norway Has Closed Its Last Coal Mine, Ending a Way of Life in the Arctic
articles.description: Svalbard has a mining history that goes back over a century. But this icy archipelago is now a cruise ship destination and a geopolitical hot spot.

articles.title: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
articles.description: A court threw out a report suggesting that Cyril Ramaphosa may have tried to conceal the theft of more than half a million dollars of U.S. currency.

articles.title: 6 Craft Retreats Offer Knitting, Pottery and More for All Skill Levels
articles.description: Interest in crafting hobbies, like knitting or pottery, isn’t new, but several factors in the wake of the pandemic have also made them appealing. Here are some suggestions for hands-on retreats.

articles.title: How an Iranian Ally Gained the Upper Hand in Yemen’s War
articles.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are on a winning streak, securing strategic territory as they fight Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies in an asymmetrical war of attrition.

articles.title: Defending Aden, Yemen’s Holdout Against the Houthis
articles.description: The war in Iran has reignited Yemen’s decade-old civil war. Saudi-backed troops are scrambling to defend against advancing Houthi fighters as the wounded are taken to the port city of Aden, the government’s provisional capital.

articles.title: Harry and Meghan’s Life as ‘Nonroyal Royals’ in the UK
articles.description: Six years after leaving the country, the Sussexes are back and arranging a careful program of public appearances. Will they complement the royal family, or compete with it?

articles.title: Colombia’s Leader Blames ‘Terrorist Attack’ for Power Outages
articles.description: The blackouts follow a string of violent episodes attributed to Colombia’s armed traffickers, as the country’s new president cracks down on the groups.

articles.title: Iraq’s Prime Minister Aims to Wrest More Power From Kurdistan Region
articles.description: Ali al-Zaidi, who just scored a symbolic victory against a powerful Iran-backed militia, has now moved to assert control over Kurdish border crossings and oil resources.

articles.title: National Security vs. the Stock Market
articles.description: President Trump swept aside concerns about possible espionage when he lobbied Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive.

articles.title: Solomon Islands Enters Security Treaty With Australia, in a Blow to China
articles.description: A 2022 Solomon Islands agreement with China had raised concerns it would enable Beijing to establish a military presence on the Pacific island. The new accord precludes such bases.

articles.title: Hungary Threw Open Its Secret Police Files. Let the Finger Pointing Begin.
articles.description: The communist-era files have exposed the vast network of informants that kept Hungary in the Soviet orbit. But how reliable are they?

articles.title: Thomas Markle Indicted in US on Charges of Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Materials
articles.description: Mr. Markle, 82, was indicted by a grand jury in Los Angeles and is expected to be arraigned in the coming weeks, prosecutors said.

articles.title: Trump Administration Pauses Joint Operations With Ecuador
articles.description: The administration has halted military operations while it investigates an operation by Ecuadorean forces that killed an accused gang leader.

articles.title: Pope Francis Diary Excerpts Published in New Book
articles.description: Over decades, before and after he became leader of the Roman Catholic Church, Francis recorded occasional entries about his fears and doubts.

articles.title: ‘Saturday Night Live’ Is Coming to France
articles.description: A French adaptation of the American sketch comedy institution will premiere next month on the premium channel Canal+. It comes as a British version is hitting a stride.

articles.title: Stock Markets Slip as Nvidia and A.I. Stocks Erase Some of Monday’s Rally
articles.description: Shares have veered wildly for days, pushed and pulled by the drama at Nvidia and the rise and fall of Anthropic’s stock after its blockbuster public offering.

articles.title: Trump’s Nvidia Push Shows Companies’ Importance in Global Economic War
articles.description: Presidents before him have bailed out companies in times of national crisis. Mr. Trump went further: He staked the fortunes of the United States on those of a favored chief executive.

articles.title: Houthi Attack on Skyscraper in Saudi Capital Wounds 11, Officials Say
articles.description: The people were wounded in the strike on a building in Riyadh, the Saudi authorities said. The Iran-backed militia and Saudi Arabia have been exchanging escalating attacks for weeks.

articles.title: A Lion on the Loose Near Istanbul? Not So Fast.
articles.description: Blurry surveillance footage spurred a frantic search — until the Turkish authorities said it was unclear whether the animal was the feline.

articles.title: Prince William and Kate’s Country Home Is Broken Into; 2 Men Arrested
articles.description: The men were arrested near Anmer Hall, the couple’s country retreat in Norfolk, on Monday night.

articles.title: Radio Offers Russian Troops Classic Rock, Nostalgia — and Pleas to Surrender
articles.description: What seem like frontline Russian radio stations are actually a Ukrainian psychological operation, hoping to sow despair among the Kremlin’s soldiers.

articles.title: China Investigates Chen Jining, Shanghai’s Party Leader, as Xi’s Purges Expand
articles.description: Before his abrupt downfall, the technocratic Chen Jining was seen as a future national leader in Xi Jinping’s China.

articles.title: Murder Charge Reinstated for French Police Officer in Teen’s Shooting
articles.description: The killing of Nahel Merzouk, 17, sparked nationwide unrest. The case against the officer accused of involvement has undergone repeated twists and turns.

articles.title: Death Toll From Indonesia Factory Fire Rises to 26 With Dozens Unaccounted for
articles.description: As the death toll rose to 26, one rescue worker said that more victims might be found near a stairwell in the building. The police opened a criminal investigation.

articles.title: Iranian Singer Receives 74 Lashes for Performing With No Hijab
articles.description: Parastoo Ahmadi sang without wearing the mandatory veil in a virtual concert in 2024 that spread quickly online and drew the ire of the Islamic republic authorities.

articles.title: For China, Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia Is a Mixed Blessing
articles.description: Beijing may welcome the return of the leading U.S. advocate for A.I. chip sales to China. But the saga could reinforce a Chinese push for self-reliance, analysts say.

articles.title: A U.N. Leader Focuses on the Deadly Problem of Road Safety
articles.description: Nneka Henry works for the United Nations to help develop solutions to the chaos and calamity caused by cars, motorcycles and scooters, and help drum up the resources to improve safety.

articles.title: The Return of Jensen Huang
articles.description: The Nvidia C.E.O. is back, President Trump is celebrating and markets are rallying.

articles.title: Attack Blamed on ISIS Kills 2 Syrian Security Force Members
articles.description: The assault on a security headquarters in the northeastern city of Hasakah was carried out by four militants who local officials linked to the Islamic State.

articles.title: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.description: The drop was largely driven by fewer people arriving from outside Europe. It reflects government action to restrict immigration after a public backlash.

articles.title: Seven injured, four critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
articles.description: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, while officials urged residents to leave the area.

articles.title: 440 players, three days, one venue - the Nations Championship logistics logjam
articles.description: The unprecedented demands of Nations Championship finals weekend have been met by meticulous planning.

articles.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
articles.description: A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority.
